newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish parliament to debate censure motion.
newsitem.headline: Turkish parliament to debate censure motion.

text.p: Turkey's parliament was to debate a leftist censure motion against the Islamist-led government on Tuesday, parliamentary officials said.
They said the parliament session was scheduled to begin at 3.00 p.m. (1300 GMT).
Two leftist parties brought the combined motion in response to what they described as a failure on the part of the coalition to act against threats to Turkey's secular system.
After speeches by the parties and the government, deputies were to vote on whether to proceed with the motion.
Analysts say opposition parties appear incapable of mobilising the 276 votes needed in the 550-seat parliament. Passage of the motion would bring down Erbakan's coalition which controls 278 seats.
A far-right party with seven deputies has said it will not support the motion.
The censure vote follows a string of opposition defeats last week, when parliament voted not to impeach Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller for alleged corruption.
Anti-government groups fell short by 19 votes in their best showing.
